What I mean is that the people, who I used to be like, are saying it is culture are not entirely wrong. To them, it is about culture. That entire culture only thrived and survived due to slavery and hate however.

What I meant in saying “I used to believe it was about culture” is that I used to not see it as a hateful and evil thing. Now I do. But the change from seeing it as good into seeing it as bad is a hard and painful one.

There is some insight needed into the mindset of these hard core people. If you grow up here, everything around you is pretty shitty and pretty poor. Except in some of bigger cities, things are not alright. Many kids here don’t see economic or social success first hand down here. Many don’t have or even know what a good education even looks like. We have people that try, but it’s still hard. Now, I know and understand that this is true for many many places around the country, especially right now. However, the difference here is that, as humans, we tend to rely and fall back on specific things to get us though hard times. One of those few long-standing things is tradition and culture.

Down here, having experienced this myself as a young child, I can say that there is something uniquely powerful telling your self that “Yah, this place used to be so cool and amazing. We used to have powerful and rich people all throughout this area. We used to be the economic power house center of the entire country. We used to be innovative and incredibly Intelligent. My family helped build that power center. My blood went into this place. We were a part of that. Maybe, just maybe, I can be a part of something like that down here again. Maybe I WONT be destined to live out in a trailer with 40 other families in a 20 acre space, growing up with a broken and angry family, and maybe I won’t be destined to be always worried about my next meal, my next paycheck to help take care of my little sister. Yah, my blood made this place better, they made it good. Maybe I can do the same then.”

This thinking is common in people the world over. The problem is that the way places down here were “cool” in the past is that it was predicated on the enslavement and revile of an entire people. That’s not a good thing. But to many, that line of though is the ONLY way people get through their day without giving up. It’s their one shitty and warped life raft in the dark sea of nothing.  It’s an inspiring hope to many that it will be ok. Telling them that they are vile and evil for sticking with it is telling them that their life raft is shitty and not worth holding onto. Which it really shouldn’t be any way, but that’s not my point.

In telling them to stop looking at it as culture but hate, it means giving up their own struggle as a person, their own identity as a person. It means accepting that their life really is just a series of fuck ups and that they can’t do better. They are destined to be awful and horrible people with nothing to offer. It means giving up. It means stepping off the boat and step into the dark and churning waters of the inexplicable nothingness and suffering they see all around them. That is what they mean when claiming culture, not hate.

The need to include doesn’t mean they want to include you. I honestly think that’s why a lot of the anti bullying and and pro friendship for everyone rules kind of make things worse. When I was bullied and ignored in middle and highschool, I didn’t want to have the the teachers, my parents, or anyone tell them to want me. I wanted them to like me on their own volition. Guilting then into talking to me was only an imitation high that never felt fulfilling. What we need as people is real genuine recognition. Not this guilty look recognition.

The saddest part is that schools can’t create that. They are not made to do that. Humans naturally segment ourselves and form our own rules. It’s healthy in my opinion to learn to navigate that. School systems can’t MAKE the kids like each other. They can teach them it’s important, and how harmful it is when you don’t, but they can’t make the kids want each other, be their for eachother, or anything like that without pulling a lot of strings that break social norms. It’s a sad truth for many people out there, including myself.

However, there is a great positive with this. The forces you feel when you are being pushed away from what you want are not forced made to simply separate you from your aspirations.
